newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No decision on Royale Belge future - GBL.
newsitem.headline: No decision on Royale Belge future - GBL.

text.p: Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) said on Tuesday it had taken no decision on the future of insurer Royale Belge.

Jean Pierre de Launoit, vice chairman of the GBL board, said at the annual shareholders' meeting, "The merger between (French insurers) AXA and UAP...has not changed anything in the joint control (of Royale Belge) which has existed since 1987 and which works satisfactorily."

"For the future nothing formal has been decided. Discussions are going on in a harmonious climate...aiming at a global solution. Whatever outcome arises should help the further development of Royal Belge and its shareholders."

There has been intense speculation ahead of Royale Belge's annual shareholders meeting this Wednesday that the company, and with it its 12.4 percent stake in bank BBL, was about to be sold by French parent AXA-UAP.
One newspaper cited Dutch financial services group ING and Swiss insurer Winterthur as suitors.
AXA-UAP and ING declined to comment.
AXA and UAP's decision at the end of 1996 to merge left AXA-UAP with two separate Belgian units, Royale Belge and AXA Belgium, a situation the group appears to be unhappy with.
Both companies' formal position is that all options remain open.
GBL owns 25.1 percent of Royale Vendome, an intermediate holding company between AXA-UAP and Royale Belge.
